records.gloss: The song of the ascents. Remember, YHWH, for David all his being afflicted,
pieces: A song of ascents. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember David and all the hardship he went through,

L.1: A song of ascents. Remember, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, for David all his affliction,

R.1: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember David and all the trouble he went through.

decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a psalm of the ark and of David's line
decisions.reason: The psalm recalls David's care to bring the ark of the LORD to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6) and the LORD's promise of a lasting line of kings (2 Samuel 7:11-16). Verses 8-10 are nearly the same as the end of Solomon's prayer at the temple (2 Chronicles 6:41-42).

decisions.choice: his being afflicted: the hardship he endured
decisions.reason: The word (a passive infinitive of 'anah) means being afflicted or humbled. It may be the troubles of David's life, or the hardship he took on himself by his vow (verses 3-5).

decisions.choice: remember for David: remember in his favor
decisions.reason: To remember something "for" someone is to keep it in mind and act on it for their good (Nehemiah 5:19; 13:31).

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 120:1.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s oath to David and his choice of Zion

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִ֭שְׁבַּע לַיהוָ֑ה נָ֝דַ֗ר לַאֲבִ֥יר יַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: how he swore to YHWH, vowed to [the] Mighty One of Jacob,
pieces: how he made an oath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and a vow to the Mighty One of Jacob,

L.2: how he swore to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob,

R.2: He made a promise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He made a solemn vow to the Mighty God of Jacob.

decisions.choice: the Mighty One of Jacob: a title of God
decisions.reason: The title ('Avir Ya'aqov) first appears in Jacob's blessing (Genesis 49:24; also Isaiah 49:26). It names God as the strong protector of Jacob's family.
The vow is not recorded elsewhere; 2 Samuel 7:1-2 tells of David's wish to build a house for the ark. The words of the vow follow in verses 3-5.
Readable makes plain that the title names God.

records.source: אִם־אָ֭בֹא בְּאֹ֣הֶל בֵּיתִ֑י אִם־אֶ֝עֱלֶ֗ה עַל־עֶ֥רֶשׂ יְצוּעָֽי׃
records.gloss: If I go into [the] tent of my house, if I go up onto [the] couch of my bed,
pieces: "I will not set foot in my own house or climb into my bed,

L.3: "I will not go into the tent of my house, nor go up onto the couch of my bed,

R.3: He said, "I will not go home, and I will not go to bed.

decisions.choice: if I go: I will not go
decisions.reason: "If" ('im) begins an oath whose curse is left unsaid ("may God punish me if ..."), so it means a strong "I will not". It is repeated in verse 4.

decisions.choice: the tent of my house: my home
decisions.reason: "Tent" is an old word for a home, kept from Israel's life in tents (2 Samuel 20:1).
Readable shows where David's words begin.

records.gloss: if I give sleep to my eyes, to my eyelids slumber,
pieces: I will not let my eyes sleep or my eyelids close,

L.4: I will not give sleep to my eyes, [or] slumber to my eyelids,

R.4: I will not sleep or even close my eyes.

decisions.choice: no sleep to my eyes: no rest at all
decisions.reason: The same words are used of urgent business that cannot wait (Proverbs 6:4). David will not rest until the ark has a home.

records.source: עַד־אֶמְצָ֣א מָ֭קוֹם לַיהוָ֑ה מִ֝שְׁכָּנ֗וֹת לַאֲבִ֥יר יַעֲקֹֽב׃
records.gloss: until I find a place for YHWH, a dwelling for [the] Mighty One of Jacob.
pieces: until I have found {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} a place to stay, a home for the Mighty One of Jacob."

L.5: until I find a place for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob."

R.5: I will rest only when I have found a place for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to live, a home for the Mighty God of Jacob."

decisions.choice: a dwelling: a home for God
decisions.reason: The word (mishkanot) is plural in form, as often for a single dwelling (43:3; 46:5). It is the word from which "tabernacle" comes.

decisions.choice: a place for the LORD: a home for the ark
decisions.reason: The ark was the sign of the LORD's presence. David brought it to Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:12-17) and wanted to build it a house (2 Samuel 7:2); Solomon built the temple on the place David had prepared (2 Chronicles 3:1).
Readable joins this verse to the vow of verses 3-4.

records.gloss: Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in [the] fields of Jaar.
pieces: Listen! We heard of it in Ephrathah, and came across it in the fields of Jaar.

L.6: Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the fields of Jaar.

R.6: We heard about the ark when we were in Ephrathah. We found it in the fields near Jaar.

decisions.reason: "It" is feminine and is not named. It is most likely the ark, named in verse 8 (the word for ark is sometimes feminine, 2 Chronicles 8:11); some take it as the place David was looking for.

Ephrathah is the district of Bethlehem, David's home (Ruth 4:11; Micah 5:1). Jaar ("forest") is probably Kiriath-jearim, "town of forests", where the ark stayed for twenty years until David brought it up (1 Samuel 7:1-2; 2 Samuel 6:2).
The people speak as those who heard of the ark in David's home country and went to fetch it.
Readable names what "it" most likely is (m1).

records.gloss: Let us go to his dwelling; let us bow down at [the] footstool of his feet.
pieces: Come, we will enter {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home and bow down before the footstool under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.

L.7: Let us go into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dwelling; let us bow down at the footstool of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet.

R.7: Let us go to the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives. Let us bow down in worship at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} footstool.

decisions.reason: The ark is called God's footstool (1 Chronicles 28:2; 99:5): the LORD is pictured as enthroned above it, with the ark at his feet.
The verb is to bow low to the ground, the posture of worship before a king or God.

records.source: קוּמָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה לִמְנוּחָתֶ֑ךָ אַ֝תָּ֗ה וַאֲר֥וֹן עֻזֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Arise, YHWH, to your resting place, you and [the] ark of your strength.
pieces: Rise up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! Come to the place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will rest, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and the ark of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} might.

L.8: Arise, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} resting place, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and the ark of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strength.

R.8: Get up, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! Come to the place where {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will rest. Come with the ark that shows how strong {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

decisions.choice: Arise, LORD: the cry when the ark set out
decisions.reason: "Arise, LORD" was said when the ark set out in the wilderness (Numbers 10:35). Now the ark is asked to come to its resting place. Verses 8-10 close Solomon's prayer in 2 Chronicles 6:41-42.
The word (menuchah) is a place of rest after travel. After its journeys the ark is to settle in Zion, which God calls "my resting place" in verse 14.

decisions.choice: the ark of your strength: the sign of your power
decisions.reason: The ark went before Israel in battle and showed the LORD's power (78:61; 1 Samuel 4-6).
As at 3:8 and elsewhere.

records.gloss: Your priests — may they be clothed [with] righteousness, and your faithful ones may they shout for joy.
pieces: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} priests be dressed in righteousness, and let those loyal to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cry out with joy.

L.9: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} priests be clothed [with] righteousness, and let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful ones shout for joy.

R.9: May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} priests always do what is right, as if it were the clothes they wear. May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful people shout for joy!

decisions.choice: clothed with righteousness: marked by it
decisions.reason: Being clothed with a quality means it covers the person and can be seen (Job 29:14; Isaiah 61:10). The priests' robes are to show a life that is right.

decisions.choice: faithful ones: those loyal to God
decisions.reason: The word (chasidim) comes from chesed, loyal love: people who are loyal to God and his covenant.
God answers this prayer in verse 16, using the same words: he will clothe the priests with salvation, and the faithful will shout for joy.

decisions.choice: always do what is right, as if it were the clothes they wear
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m1).

records.source: בַּ֭עֲבוּר דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ אַל־תָּ֝שֵׁ֗ב פְּנֵ֣י מְשִׁיחֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: For the sake of David your servant, not turn away [the] face of your anointed.
pieces: Because of David {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, do not refuse the king {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have anointed.

L.10: For the sake of David {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, do not turn away the face of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anointed.

R.10: Because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant David, do not turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} back on the king {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have anointed.

decisions.choice: turn away the face: refuse a request
decisions.reason: To turn away someone's face is to send them away with their request refused (1 Kings 2:16-20).

Kings were anointed with oil when they began to reign (1 Samuel 16:13). The word (mashiach) is the source of "Messiah". Here it is the reigning king of David's line; later readers, including the New Testament, heard in it the promised king.

decisions.choice: your servant: one chosen to serve God
decisions.reason: "Servant" is a title of honor for David (2 Samuel 7:5; 89:4).
Balanced and Readable say who the anointed one is (m2).

records.source: נִשְׁבַּֽע־יְהוָ֨ה׀לְדָוִ֡ד אֱמֶת֮ לֹֽא־יָשׁ֪וּב מִ֫מֶּ֥נָּה מִפְּרִ֥י בִטְנְךָ֑ אָ֝שִׁ֗ית לְכִסֵּא־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: YHWH has sworn to David [in] truth; not he will turn back from it: From [the] fruit of your body I will set on the throne for you.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has given David {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word on oath, a true word {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will never take back: "I will place a child of your own body on your throne.

L.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has sworn to David [in] truth; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not turn back from it: "[One] from the fruit of your body I will set on your throne.

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made David a firm promise, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will never go back on it. He said, "I will make one of your own children king after you.

decisions.reason: The LORD's answer echoes David's oath (verse 2): David swore to the LORD, and the LORD swears to David. The promise is the one in 2 Samuel 7:12-16, also recalled in 89:4-5 and 89:36-38.
Peter says that David knew God had sworn with an oath to seat one of his descendants on his throne, and so foresaw the resurrection of the Messiah (Acts 2:30).
The word ('emet) means what is firm and can be relied on: the oath will stand.

decisions.choice: the fruit of your body: your descendant
decisions.reason: "Fruit of the body" means a person's children and descendants (127:3; Deuteronomy 7:13).
Readable shows where the LORD's words begin.

records.source: אִֽם־יִשְׁמְר֬וּ בָנֶ֨יךָ׀בְּרִיתִי֮ וְעֵדֹתִ֥י ז֗וֹ אֲלַ֫מְּדֵ֥ם גַּם־בְּנֵיהֶ֥ם עֲדֵי־עַ֑ד יֵ֝שְׁב֗וּ לְכִסֵּא־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: If your sons keep my covenant and my testimonies which I will teach them, also their sons until forever will sit on the throne for you.
pieces: If your sons are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant and to the decrees I will teach them, their sons as well will sit on your throne for all time."

L.12: If your sons keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} testimonies which I will teach them, their sons also will sit on your throne forever and ever."

R.12: If your sons are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant and obey the laws I teach them, then their sons will also sit on your throne forever."

decisions.reason: The promise to David's line is lasting (2 Samuel 7:14-16), but each king must keep the covenant to enjoy it (1 Kings 2:4; 89:31-38). Kings who broke it were punished, yet the line was not cut off for ever.
The word ('edot) is the solemn charge of God's law, as in 119 ("decrees" at Balanced).
The covenant (berit) is the LORD's bond with David and his line, with promises on God's side and loyalty asked on theirs (89:4, 29).
As in Psalm 119, "testimonies" at Literal and "decrees" at Balanced; Readable says "laws", which reads more simply in the LORD's own words.

records.source: כִּֽי־בָחַ֣ר יְהוָ֣ה בְּצִיּ֑וֹן אִ֝וָּ֗הּ לְמוֹשָׁ֥ב לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For YHWH has chosen Zion; he has desired it for a dwelling for himself.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} chose Zion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} longed to make it {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home.

L.13: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen Zion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has desired it for a dwelling for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has chosen Zion. He wanted it to be the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives.

decisions.reason: The LORD's choice of Zion as the place for his name goes with his choice of David (78:68-70; Deuteronomy 12:5). It is the reason for the promises that follow.

decisions.choice: desired: wanted it for his own
decisions.reason: The verb ('avah) is a strong wish. It is repeated in verse 14.

records.gloss: This [is] my resting place until forever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.
pieces: "Here is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} resting place for all time; I will live here, for this is the place I longed for.

L.14: "This [is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} resting place forever and ever; here I will dwell, for I have desired it.

R.14: He says, "This will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} place of rest forever. I will live here, because this is the place I wanted.

decisions.reason: From here to the end of the psalm the LORD speaks, answering the prayer of verses 8-10 point by point.
The verb (yashav) means to sit or live; said of God it often means to sit enthroned (2:4; 123:1).

decisions.choice: my resting place: the answer to verse 8
decisions.reason: The prayer asked the LORD to come to his resting place (verse 8); he says that Zion is that place.
Readable shows that the LORD is speaking (m1).

records.source: צֵ֭ידָהּ בָּרֵ֣ךְ אֲבָרֵ֑ךְ אֶ֝בְיוֹנֶ֗יהָ אַשְׂבִּ֥יעַֽ לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: Its provisions I will surely bless; its needy I will satisfy [with] bread.
pieces: I will richly bless the city's food supply; I will give its poor all the bread they need.

L.15: Its provisions I will abundantly bless; its needy I will satisfy [with] bread.

R.15: I will bless Zion with plenty of food. I will give its poor people all the bread they want.

decisions.choice: bless I will bless: a strong promise
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled (an infinitive with the finite verb) for emphasis: "I will surely, richly bless".
"Its" (feminine) refers to Zion, the city of verse 13.
Balanced and Readable name the city at the start of God's promises (m2).

records.source: וְֽ֭כֹהֲנֶיהָ אַלְבִּ֣ישׁ יֶ֑שַׁע וַ֝חֲסִידֶ֗יהָ רַנֵּ֥ן יְרַנֵּֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And its priests I will clothe [with] salvation, and its faithful ones will surely shout for joy.
pieces: I will dress its priests in salvation, and its faithful people will shout and sing for joy.

L.16: And its priests I will clothe [with] salvation, and its faithful ones will shout aloud for joy.

R.16: Its priests will wear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} salvation like clothing. Its faithful people will shout and sing for joy.

decisions.reason: Verse 9 asked that the priests be clothed with righteousness; God promises to clothe them with salvation, his rescue and help. The faithful will shout for joy, as was asked, and the verb is doubled for emphasis.
The word (yesha') is help that saves from danger, and the safety that follows.
Readable says whose salvation it is; the LORD is speaking.

records.source: שָׁ֤ם אַצְמִ֣יחַ קֶ֣רֶן לְדָוִ֑ד עָרַ֥כְתִּי נֵ֝֗ר לִמְשִׁיחִֽי׃
records.gloss: There I will make sprout a horn for David; I have set in order a lamp for my anointed.
pieces: There I will make David's horn sprout up; I have trimmed a lamp for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anointed king.

L.17: There I will make a horn sprout for David; I have set in order a lamp for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anointed.

R.17: There I will raise up a powerful king from David's family. I will keep the lamp of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anointed king burning, so that his family line will go on.

decisions.choice: a horn: strength, a strong king
decisions.reason: A horn is a picture of strength, like the horns of a wild ox (89:18, 25; 1 Samuel 2:10). To make a horn sprout for David is to raise up a strong king of his line. Zechariah's song speaks of "a horn of salvation in the house of David" (Luke 1:69).
The verb (tsamach) is used of plants. The prophets call the coming king of David's line the "Branch" (tsemach) from the same root (Jeremiah 23:5; 33:15).

decisions.choice: a lamp: a line that goes on
decisions.reason: A lamp left burning means a family that has not died out. God kept a lamp for David in Jerusalem by keeping his descendants on the throne (1 Kings 11:36; 15:4; 2 Kings 8:19).

decisions.choice: a powerful king; so that his family line will go on
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two pictures mean (m1, m3).

records.source: א֭וֹיְבָיו אַלְבִּ֣ישׁ בֹּ֑שֶׁת וְ֝עָלָ֗יו יָצִ֥יץ נִזְרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: His enemies I will clothe [with] shame, but on him will shine his crown.
pieces: I will dress his enemies in shame, but the crown on his head will gleam."

L.18: His enemies I will clothe [with] shame, but on him his crown will shine."

R.18: I will cover his enemies with shame. But the crown on his head will shine brightly."

decisions.reason: The verb (tsits) can mean to shine or to blossom; it follows the picture of sprouting in verse 17. The same root names the gold plate on the high priest's turban (Exodus 28:36).
The psalm ends its pictures of clothing (verses 9, 16): the priests wear salvation, the enemies wear shame, the king a shining crown.
"His" and "him" are the anointed king of verse 17, David's descendant.
